item.text:
Yes. ResStock’s **Geometry Wall Type data for Maine is incorrect** because of mislabeled county tax assessor data. For example, the report identifies an implausible distribution for Maine’s single-family detached homes: about 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete/CMU. The issue report says no fix has been implemented and that **all published ResStock datasets are believed to be affected**. See the [ResStock issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html).

The report recommends:

- **For wall type or wall exterior finish distributions:** use nearby-state results, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For measures whose applicability depends on wall type:** either reweight Maine results using nearby-state wall type distributions or use nearby-state results directly.

This can affect wall insulation upgrade applicability, since some measures apply only to wood-frame walls. The team currently does **not** believe baseline or upgrade energy consumption, emissions, or energy bill results are significantly affected. These findings and recommendations appear in the [release-pinned copy of the issue report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NatLabRockies/buildstock-corpus/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1-v1/processed/resstock/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1/github_site/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.md).
